name: Multiple Visa -- Investment and Business Activity

requirements.blocker_text: Per Bolivia's own Foreign Ministry consular portal, the 'Visa Múltiple' authorizes repeated entry/exit for investment and business activities, valid 1 year, with stays not exceeding 90 consecutive days per entry. NO minimum investment amount is specified anywhere this dataset could find -- one tier-4 legal-services source states explicitly that 'Bolivia doesn't require a minimum investment amount' for this category, a genuine and disclosed absence rather than an unresearched gap. This is a materially different structure from Paraguay's SUACE program (a fixed USD 70,000 threshold with a named job-creation requirement) -- Bolivia's investor route appears to rest on demonstrating genuine business/investment activity rather than a quantified capital bar.
requirements.fix_path: Demonstrate genuine investment or business activity in Bolivia and apply for the Visa Múltiple at a consulate.

evidence_required.document: Evidence of investment or business activity

outcome.duration_length: 1 year, renewable (90 consecutive days per entry)

sources.title: Bolivian Foreign Ministry consular portal -- confirms the Visa Múltiple category for investment/business, its 1-year/90-day structure
Armenian Lawyer (immigration-law blog) -- explicit statement that Bolivia requires no minimum investment amount for investor entry

This is a genuinely different market position from every other 'business' category file built earlier in this session (Iraq's KRG investor confirmation, Paraguay's SUACE, Afghanistan's not-yet-implemented proposal) -- Bolivia's is a real, currently operative visa with essentially no investment bar, but also with no residency payoff attached to it.
